answers.label: Q1
answers.solution:
Multiply the two brackets that form a difference of squares first:
\((2x + 1)(2x - 1) = (2x)^2 - 1^2 = 4x^2 - 1\)
Now multiply by \((x + 2)\):
\((4x^2 - 1)(x + 2) = 4x^3 + 8x^2 - x - 2\)

So, \((2x+1)(x+2)(2x-1) = 4x^3 + 8x^2 - x - 2\).

answers.solution:
\(25x^4 - y^4 = (5x^2)^2 - (y^2)^2\)
Using \(a^2 - b^2 = (a - b)(a + b)\):
\(= (5x^2 - y^2)(5x^2 + y^2)\)
Neither factor splits further with whole-number coefficients.

So, \(25x^4 - y^4 = (5x^2 - y^2)(5x^2 + y^2)\).

answers.solution:
The wording "17 m North-East and 8 m South" is unclear as printed. The numbers 17 and 8 point to a right-angled triangle in which his 17 m walk is the slanting side (hypotenuse) and his 8 m walk south is one side; his distance from the start is the third side.
By Pythagoras' theorem:
Distance\(^2 = 17^2 - 8^2 = 289 - 64 = 225\)
Distance \(= \sqrt{225} = 15\) m
(If the 17 m walk is taken exactly along the North-East direction at 45 degrees, the distance comes out as \(\sqrt{353 - 136\sqrt{2}} \approx 12.7\) m, which is not a value a calculator-free paper would set.)

So, Mohan is 15 m from his initial position.

answers.solution:
Area of square ABCD \(= 28 \times 28 = 784\) cm\(^2\)
Semicircle BPC has diameter BC = 28 cm, so radius = 14 cm; its lowest point P is 14 cm below BC, the centre of the square.
Area of semicircle \(= \frac{1}{2} \times \frac{22}{7} \times 14 \times 14 = 308\) cm\(^2\)
Triangle APD has base AD = 28 cm and height = distance of P from AD = 14 cm.
Area of triangle APD \(= \frac{1}{2} \times 28 \times 14 = 196\) cm\(^2\)
The semicircle and the triangle meet only at P, and what is left of the square is exactly the two shaded parts.
Shaded area \(= 784 - 308 - 196 = 280\) cm\(^2\)

So, the area of the shaded region is 280 cm\(^2\).

\(2 = 2\), \(4 = 2^2\), \(9 = 3^2\)
LCM \(= 2^2 \times 3^2 = 36\)

The largest 4-digit number is 9999.
Divide 9999 by 411: \(411 \times 24 = 9864\), remainder \(9999 - 9864 = 135\).
Subtract the remainder: \(9999 - 135 = 9864\)

So, the largest 4-digit number exactly divisible by 411 is 9864.

Let the radii be \(R\) and \(r\).
\(\pi R^2 = 15 \times \pi r^2\)
\(\frac{R^2}{r^2} = 15\), so \(\frac{R}{r} = \sqrt{15}\)
Ratio of circumferences \(= \frac{2\pi R}{2\pi r} = \frac{R}{r} = \sqrt{15} : 1\)
(The figure 15 gives an awkward root; if the paper meant 16 times, the ratio would be 4 : 1. The method is the same: the ratio of circumferences is the square root of the ratio of areas.)

So, the ratio of their circumferences is \(\sqrt{15} : 1\).

Length of wire = perimeter of the triangle \(= 3 \times 4.18 = 12.54\) cm
The same wire makes the ring, so circumference \(= \pi d = 12.54\)
\(\frac{22}{7} \times d = 12.54\)
\(d = \frac{12.54 \times 7}{22} = \frac{87.78}{22} = 3.99\) cm

So, the diameter of the ring is 3.99 cm.

answers.label: Q12
answers.solution:
"Value of copper" is read as the volume of copper, since no price is given.
Outer radius \(R = 5\) cm, inner radius \(r = 3\) cm, length \(h = 210\) cm.
Volume of copper \(= \pi R^2 h - \pi r^2 h = \pi h (R^2 - r^2)\)
\(= \frac{22}{7} \times 210 \times (25 - 9)\)
\(= 22 \times 30 \times 16 = 10560\) cm\(^3\)

So, the copper used is 10560 cm\(^3\).

\(\frac{5^5 \times 3^{-5}}{125 \times 6^{-5} \times 10^{-1}} = \frac{5^5 \times 6^5 \times 10}{125 \times 3^5}\)
\(\frac{6^5}{3^5} = 2^5 = 32\) and \(\frac{5^5}{125} = \frac{5^5}{5^3} = 5^2 = 25\)
Value \(= 25 \times 32 \times 10 = 8000\)

So, the expression simplifies to 8000.

Let Ram's present age be \(x\) years.
After 14 years: \(x + 14\). Four years ago: \(x - 4\).
\(x + 14 = 3(x - 4)\)
\(x + 14 = 3x - 12\)
\(26 = 2x\), so \(x = 13\)
Check: after 14 years he will be 27, and four years ago he was 9; \(27 = 3 \times 9\).

So, Ram is 13 years old now.

So, \(x = -1\).

answers.solution:
Let the number of Rs 5 coins be \(x\). Then the number of Rs 2 coins is \(3x\).
Total money: \(5 \times x + 2 \times 3x = 77\)
\(5x + 6x = 77\)
\(11x = 77\), so \(x = 7\)
Rs 2 coins \(= 3 \times 7 = 21\)
Check: \(7 \times 5 + 21 \times 2 = 35 + 42 = 77\).

So, he has 7 coins of Rs 5 and 21 coins of Rs 2.

Let the speed of the boat in still water be \(x\) km/hr.
Downstream speed \(= x + 3\), upstream speed \(= x - 3\).
The distance is the same both ways:
\(5(x + 3) = 6(x - 3)\)
\(5x + 15 = 6x - 18\)
\(x = 33\)
Check: downstream \(36 \times 5 = 180\) km, upstream \(30 \times 6 = 180\) km.

So, the speed of the boat in still water is 33 km/hr.

18 men bind 900 books in 10 days.
Books bound by 1 man in 1 day \(= \frac{900}{18 \times 10} = 5\)
To bind 600 books in 12 days, books needed per day \(= \frac{600}{12} = 50\)
Number of binders \(= \frac{50}{5} = 10\)
(Or: \(\text{men} = 18 \times \frac{600}{900} \times \frac{10}{12} = 10\).)

So, 10 binders will be required.

Time for first part \(= \frac{100}{50} = 2\) hours
Time for second part \(= \frac{120}{54} = \frac{20}{9}\) hours
Time for last part \(= \frac{30}{60} = \frac{1}{2}\) hour
Total time \(= 2 + \frac{20}{9} + \frac{1}{2} = \frac{36 + 40 + 9}{18} = \frac{85}{18}\) hours
Total distance \(= 100 + 120 + 30 = 250\) km
Average speed \(= \frac{250}{\frac{85}{18}} = \frac{250 \times 18}{85} = \frac{900}{17} = 52\frac{16}{17}\) km/hr

So, his average speed is \(52\frac{16}{17}\) km/hr, about 52.94 km/hr.

First three-fourths of the journey \(= \frac{3}{4} \times 320 = 240\) km
Time taken for it at 60 km/hr \(= \frac{240}{60} = 4\) hours
Remaining distance \(= 320 - 240 = 80\) km
Remaining time \(= 4\frac{3}{4} - 4 = \frac{3}{4}\) hour
Speed for the rest \(= \frac{80}{\frac{3}{4}} = \frac{320}{3} = 106\frac{2}{3}\) km/hr

So, the speed for the balance of the journey is \(106\frac{2}{3}\) km/hr.

answers.label: Q26
answers.solution:
Long division of \(3x^5 + 7x^4 - 11x^3 + 8x^2 - 32x + 5\) by \(x^2 + 3x + 2\):
Step 1: \(\frac{3x^5}{x^2} = 3x^3\); \(3x^3(x^2 + 3x + 2) = 3x^5 + 9x^4 + 6x^3\); subtract: \(-2x^4 - 17x^3 + 8x^2\)
Step 2: \(\frac{-2x^4}{x^2} = -2x^2\); \(-2x^2(x^2 + 3x + 2) = -2x^4 - 6x^3 - 4x^2\); subtract: \(-11x^3 + 12x^2 - 32x\)
Step 3: \(\frac{-11x^3}{x^2} = -11x\); \(-11x(x^2 + 3x + 2) = -11x^3 - 33x^2 - 22x\); subtract: \(45x^2 - 10x + 5\)
Step 4: \(\frac{45x^2}{x^2} = 45\); \(45(x^2 + 3x + 2) = 45x^2 + 135x + 90\); subtract: \(-145x - 85\)
The remainder has a lower degree than the divisor, so we stop.
Check at \(x = 1\): dividend \(= -20\); divisor \(\times\) quotient + remainder \(= 6 \times 35 - 230 = -20\).

So, the quotient is \(3x^3 - 2x^2 - 11x + 45\) and the remainder is \(-145x - 85\).

Let the tens digit be \(a\) and the units digit \(b\). The number is \(10a + b\); reversed it is \(10b + a\).
\((10a + b) + (10b + a) = 143\)
\(11(a + b) = 143\), so \(a + b = 13\)
The digits differ by 3: \(a - b = 3\) or \(b - a = 3\).
If \(a - b = 3\): \(2a = 16\), \(a = 8\), \(b = 5\), number 85.
If \(b - a = 3\): \(a = 5\), \(b = 8\), number 58.
Check: \(85 + 58 = 143\).

So, the original number is 85 or 58 (both satisfy the conditions).

(i) Through X draw a line XF parallel to AB (and so parallel to DE).
\(\angle ABX + \angle BXF = 180^\circ\) (co-interior angles, \(AB \parallel XF\)), so the part of the angle at X next to B \(= 180^\circ - 120^\circ = 60^\circ\) from the line XF on the left.
\(\angle EDX + \angle DXF' = 180^\circ\) (co-interior angles, \(DE \parallel XF\)), so the part next to D \(= 180^\circ - 95^\circ = 85^\circ\) from the line XF on the right.
The three angles at X on the line through X add to \(180^\circ\):
\(60^\circ + x + 85^\circ = 180^\circ\)
\(x = 35^\circ\)

(ii) In triangle QRS, \(\angle QSE\) is the exterior angle at S, so it equals the sum of the two opposite interior angles:
\(\angle QRS + \angle RQS = \angle QSE\)
\(x + 40^\circ = 75^\circ\), so \(x = 35^\circ\)
Since \(PQ \parallel RS\) and \(\angle QPR = 90^\circ\), \(\angle PRS = 180^\circ - 90^\circ = 90^\circ\) (co-interior angles).
\(y + x = 90^\circ\), so \(y = 90^\circ - 35^\circ = 55^\circ\)

So, (i) \(x = 35^\circ\); (ii) \(x = 35^\circ\) and \(y = 55^\circ\).
